title: Finite morphisms
statement:
Let $u:V\to W$ be finite [sk-def-conv]. For an abelian sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and a geometric point
$\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to W$, with $\Omega$ algebraically
closed [def-weil-geometric-point], one has

$$
(u_*F)_{\bar w}\simeq
\prod_{\substack{\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)\to V\\ u\bar v=\bar w}}F_{\bar v}.
$$

Here stalks are [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], direct image is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the indexing set is the geometric fibre [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. The product is finite. The functor $u_*$ on abelian sheaves is exact, and its
formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Consequently, for every base
change $W'\to W$ and every constant commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$, the derived
exchange [sk-def-exchange] is an isomorphism in $D^+(W'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ for
every $K\in D^+(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$, with the module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] to $u:V\to W$, $F$, and $\bar w$. Its set $P(\bar w)$ is exactly the indexing set in the statement, it is finite, and its isomorphism has component $r_{u,\bar v,F}:(u_*F)_{\bar w}\to F_{\bar v}$ given by restriction of germs. This proves the displayed formula, including finiteness. These maps are natural in $F$: applying a morphism of sheaves to a representative section before taking its germ gives the same result as applying its stalk map afterward. This uses only the sectionwise definition of the map $u_*F\to u_*G$ in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus a sequence is carried on stalks to the corresponding finite product of sequences. The cited finite-stalk lemma packages the blueprint's strict-henselization calculation, rather than requiring a new copy of that calculation here.

Let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $V_{\Et}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] each sequence at $\bar v$ is short exact. Under the natural formula of step 1, the sequence of stalks of its direct image is their finite product. It is short exact: kernels and injectivity are checked coordinate by coordinate, and a tuple in the product of the $C_{\bar v}$ has a lift obtained by choosing a lift in each of the finitely many $B_{\bar v}$. The empty product is the zero group and has the same property. Direct image is already additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $Q=\operatorname{coker}(u_*B\to u_*C)$, exactness of stalks gives $Q_{\bar w}=0$ for every $\bar w$. The map $0\to Q$ is therefore an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], so $Q=0$. This proves that $u_*$ is exact.

Write a base-change square as $V'\xrightarrow{g'}V$, $u':V'\to W'$, $g:W'\to W$, with $ug'=gu'$. Its cartesian identification is [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The morphism $u'$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), so steps 1 and 2 apply to it. Fix $\bar w':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and put $\bar w=g\bar w'$. The map $\bar v'\mapsto g'\bar v'$ is a bijection from the lifts of $\bar w'$ through $u'$ to the lifts of $\bar w$ through $u$: its inverse sends $\bar v$ to the unique map with projections $(\bar v,\bar w')$, given by the fibre-product universal property. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], the stalk of $g^{-1}u_*F$ at $\bar w'$ identifies with $(u_*F)_{\bar w}$, and the factor $(g'^{-1}F)_{\bar v'}$ identifies with $F_{g'\bar v'}$. Consequently both sides of the underived exchange identify with the finite product $\prod_{u\bar v=\bar w}F_{\bar v}$. It remains to check the actual exchange map under these identifications.

Use the representative formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. A germ in the source of step 3, after the inverse-image stalk identification, is represented by $s\in(u_*F)(U)=F(V\times_WU)$ at a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar a)$ of $\bar w$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. To represent its inverse-image germ at $\bar w'$, pull $s$ back to $U'=U\times_WW'$ through the adjunction unit. The exchange sends this representative to the unit pullback of $s$ on $V'\times_{W'}U'$, using its canonical map to $V\times_WU$. At the point $\bar v'$ over $\bar w'$, restriction to its germ is the $\bar v'$-component of the target finite-stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction]. The unit-germ formula of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to $g'$, sends this germ to the germ of the original $s$ at $(V\times_WU,(g'\bar v',\bar a))$. That is precisely $r_{u,g'\bar v',F}$ of the original germ. Every source germ has such a representative, so each coordinate of the exchange is this identity after the reindexing of step 3. Hence it is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, and therefore an isomorphism of sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. This proves compatibility with arbitrary base change, including the specified map, not merely the existence of an isomorphism of its endpoints.

Now let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring and work with sheaves of modules over its constant sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting to abelian sheaves is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels. It also reflects zero objects (the identity of an object with underlying zero sheaf is zero by faithfulness), and therefore reflects exactness and isomorphisms. By the module clause of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], module direct image commutes with this forgetful functor. Thus step 2 proves exactness of both $u_*$ and $u'_* $ on module sheaves. Inverse image is exact and its underlying abelian functor, unit and counit agree with the abelian ones by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear] identifies the module underived exchange with the same map after forgetting. Step 4 and reflection of isomorphisms prove that it is an isomorphism of module sheaves, natural in the module sheaf. This uses no torsion or invertibility hypothesis on $\Lambda$.

proof.text:
For $K\in D^+(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ choose a bounded below injective representative $K\simeq QI$ as supplied by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and choose an injective replacement $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$. The resolution clause of [sk-def-exchange], made precise for the same module mate by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-module-termwise], identifies the specified derived exchange, up to its canonical source and target isomorphisms, with the localization of
$$g^{-1}u_*I\xrightarrow{\Ex^0_I}u'_*g'^{-1}I\xrightarrow{u'_*(j)}u'_*J.$$
The first arrow is a morphism of complexes by naturality and is an isomorphism in every degree by step 5, hence is an isomorphism of complexes (the degreewise inverses commute with the differentials). The functor $u'_*$ is exact by step 5; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] implies that it computes its derived functor on every complex and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $u'_*(j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Both arrows become isomorphisms after localization, so the exchange of [sk-def-exchange] is an isomorphism with the required endpoints in $D^+(W'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. No preservation of injectives by $g'^{-1}$ is asserted or needed.
